identity.title: ALMA Detection of Dark Chromospheric Holes in the Quiet Sun

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of a quiet-Sun region at a wavelength of 3 mm, obtained during the first solar ALMA cycle on April 27, 2017

evidence.quote: A single quiet-Sun target about 200$''$ south-west of disk center, tracked for solar rotation

question.value: Does ALMA Band 3 reveal quiet-Sun chromospheric structure, in particular dark/cool regions, that is not seen in UV, visible or magnetogram data?

evidence.quote: report the first detection of particular dark (i.e. cool) regions in ALMA images
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: $ADS/JAO.ALMA\#2016.1.00202.S$.
acquired on 2017 April 27 in Band 3 (100 GHz, i.e., a wavelength of 3 mm) in configuration C40-3

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: four 2 GHz-wide spectral windows at 93, 95, 105 and 107 GHz

evidence.quote: The four 2 GHz-wide spectral windows at 93, 95, 105 and 107 GHz were combined in the mapping

arrays.value: 12m and 7m arrays plus total power antennae

evidence.quote: supplemented by single-dish images of the full Sun with a cadence of $\approx$ 10 minutes, made with ALMA’s total power antennae at a resolution of 60$''$
in configuration C40-3, which included 38$\times$12m antennae and 8$\times$7m antennae
then restored with a synthesized beam of 1.6$''$
observed in 10.5 minute scans separated by 2-minute calibration scans, with 2-second integrations, for a total of 37 minutes
The Sun was observed in the time interval 16:00–16:45 UT (45 minutes).
60 photospheric magnetograms with a 45-sec cadence from the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager
220 images at 1600 Å, 1700 Å, and 304 Å, obtained with a 12-sec cadence by the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly

provided.value: 82 slit-jaw images in Mg II k 2796 Å

evidence.quote: 82 IRIS slit-jaw images with a 32-sec cadence in the 2796 Å Mg II k line
38 images from the BBSO and 35 images from the GONG telescope at CTIO

pipeline_or_manual.value: standard CASA software, calibration following solar commissioning papers

evidence.quote: calibrations followed the prescriptions given therein
Individual 2-second interferometric images were mapped and self-calibrated using standard CASA software
The images were made 401 pixels square, with a cell size of 0.3$''$
The mapped field of view (FOV) was about 120$''$
corrected for the primary beam response

array_combination.value: interferometer images plus single-dish brightness offset of 7236 K added

evidence.quote: 7236 K (derived from the target location in the single-dish images) was added to each image
restored with a synthesized beam of 1.6$''$

what.value: Solar ALMA calibration and flux-to-brightness-temperature conversion follow commissioning papers

evidence.quote: Solar observing with ALMA is described in the commissioning papers by (cite: 2017SoPh..292...87S) and (cite: 2017SoPh..292...88W)

unstated_but_needed: Imaging task, deconvolver, weighting/robust, and cleaning details
How the 7236 K offset was derived from total-power maps
Co-alignment and mask details for the ROI rectangles

method.value: Per-2s images mapped, self-calibrated, converted to Tb, single-dish offset added

evidence.quote: the interferometric images were converted from flux to brightness temperature, and then 7236 K
The final data cube $T_b(x,y,t)$ contains 1090 images.

method.value: Cross-correlation of 45-min averaged images against SDO full-disk reference

evidence.quote: all other images were coaligned by cross-correlating images averaged over 45 minutes
The remaining image displacements are less than 1$''$

analysis_steps.goal: Compare time-averaged images and histograms for ChAH, network and internetwork regions

method.value: Time-averaged maps and brightness/DN histograms for four equal-size rectangles

evidence.quote: we complemented it with three other regions of the same size in the FOV

validation.value: Stability checked via histograms of full time sequence

evidence.quote: To confirm the ChAH’s stability over the duration of the observations
mapped and self-calibrated using standard CASA software

results_numeric.quantity: Minimum ALMA Band 3 Tb in ChAH

evidence.quote: in the ChAH data cube it drops as low as 4370 K, which is about 60% of the quiet-Sun brightness temperature
With horizontal dimensions of approx. 20$''$ x 20$''$

results_numeric.quantity: Fraction of frames with Tb<5000 K in ChAH rectangle

evidence.quote: In 57% of the 2s frames there are regions within the blue ChAH rectangle where the brightness temperature is below 5000 K.
The brightness temperature ranges from 5600 K to 7500 K in the Band 3 image

findings_qualitative.value: ChAH is long-lasting and not distinguishable in UV or magnetogram data; Halpha is relatively bright there

evidence.quote: the ChAH remains quite stable over the whole time series, demonstrating that it is a long lasting phenomenon

claims.hypothesis: Does ALMA detect cool chromospheric regions missed by other diagnostics?
claims.experiment: Compare Band 3 maps and histograms with HMI, AIA, IRIS, Halpha for dark, network and internetwork regions
claims.result: ChAH has histogram maximum ~1000 K below internetwork in Band 3 only
claims.finding: ALMA senses cool chromospheric gas missed by shorter-wavelength diagnostics

evidence.quote: we conclude that no other data set shows even nearly as clear a difference between ChAH and normal internetwork as ALMA does

referee_caveats_inferred: Interferometric missing flux handled by a single constant offset
Single region, single epoch; a cool-gas interpretation is speculative

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA project code cited in acknowledgments

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: $ADS/JAO.ALMA\#2016.1.00202.S$.

missing_for_reproduction: Solar ALMA imaging scripts and parameters
reproducibility.score_reason: Public data and clear region definitions, but the imaging recipe is mostly delegated to commissioning papers.
